points.titre: The word stands out in its example sentence
points.texte: On the collection cards, in the dictionary entry and in the guided tour, the word that the sentence illustrates is now written in bold. You spot it at a glance, even when the sentence uses another form of it, and it is the official dictionary itself that says which word it is: every sentence now has one, including those where nothing pointed to it before.

images.alt: The « Ameis » card of the collection, open, bearing the LuxKeyb watermark. Under the drawing of a golden ant in front of the lit façades of a town at nightfall, the plate with the word « Ameis », then the text panel: the meaning « fourmi » (ant), the example sentence « ënner dem Fënsterbriet haust eng Kolonie Ameisen » with the word « Ameisen » in bold, and its translation « une colonie de fourmis s'est installée sous le rebord de la fenêtre » (a colony of ants has settled under the window ledge).
images.legende: The card's word stands out in its sentence, even in the plural.

points.texte: When you tapped a card in the collection, it stayed hidden behind the dark veil for a moment before turning over. It now turns over almost at once, even on modest phones.
On modest phones, animated cards no longer stutter. The Ferris wheel and the carousel horses of the Schueberfouer turn smoothly again, and swiping from one card to the next happens without a pause.

points.titre: The Mëllerdall as in the photo
points.texte: The Schéissendëmpel card gets back its small moss-covered stone bridge, its three waterfalls dropping from the same pool between two large rocks, and its dark undergrowth where the light passes under the arch.
The pool is a limpid blue, and yellow irises stand with their feet in the water, which you can see through.

images.alt: The landscape of the Mëllerdall card in two views side by side, marked with the LuxKeyb watermark. 1. In the afternoon: in undergrowth of ivy and leaves, the small mossy stone bridge at the back; in front, three waterfalls drop between large green rocks into a turquoise pool where pebbles and a few fish show; in the foreground, yellow irises stand with their feet in the water. 2. The same landscape at night, all in blues, the three waterfalls lit.
images.legende: The Schéissendëmpel in the Mëllerdall, in the afternoon and at night.

points.titre: A golden autumn on every card
points.texte: Trees turn from brown to gold and keep their leaves clearly drawn, by day and by night, instead of mixed green and orange patches. Meadows and moss turn to straw, and fir trees stay green.

Its hornbeam hedge is made of real leaves, which turn russet one by one in autumn and scatter dead leaves on the lawn. Its two bronze lions, sitting face to face on either side of the stairs, raise their heads, their manes over their skulls.
At the Upper Sûre lake, on the Our and at the Haff Réimech, you can see the foot of the reeds under the surface of the water.

points.titre: The houses of the Gëlle Fra
points.texte: They stand firmly on the ground and no longer float.

images.alt: Four card landscapes in autumn, in the afternoon, marked with the LuxKeyb watermark. 1. Ansembourg: in front of the castle, two verdigris bronze lions face each other on either side of the stairs, their manes over their heads, between two hedges of yellow and russet leaves; dead leaves are scattered over the lawn. 2. Esch-Sauer: the turquoise lake bordered by russet forests; on the right, the foot of the reeds fades away under the surface of the water. 3. Vianden: the castle above the valley, orange and golden hills. 4. The Mëllerdall: the stone bridge and the waterfalls, framed by russet foliage and golden ferns.
images.legende: Ansembourg, Esch-Sauer, Vianden and the Mëllerdall in autumn.

points.titre: The Red Bridge redrawn from a photo
points.texte: The Rout Bréck has its true outline again, with its railing and its street lamps.

points.titre: Every place in its true material
points.texte: Pylons, fences and street lamps are steel, no longer gold; the Mëllerdall sandstone shows its layers; the Hohllay millstones are carved into the rock; the Schengen stelae are rusted steel; the ramparts and the Bock rock show their stones; at Ansembourg the terrace is stone, with its arches, its lions and its steps; Neimënster abbey has its slate roofs; the Gëlle Fra shines on her pink granite; the Breedewee gate is made of big stones right up to the arch; the Conzefenn fence is real wood, knots and all.

images.alt: Four card landscapes, marked with the LuxKeyb watermark, each shown in two views side by side: before on the left, after on the right. 1. Schengen: the three stelae, brown like wood, turn rust red, in steel. 2. The Gëlle Fra: her grey obelisk turns pink like granite, and the golden statue gains highlights. 3. The Mëllerdall: the smooth sandstone walls show their layers of rock. 4. Ansembourg: below the castle, the plain yellow terrace becomes a stone wall pierced with dark arches, and in front the two stone lions frame a flight of steps.
images.legende: Schengen, the Gëlle Fra, the Mëllerdall and Ansembourg, before and after.
